offers.when: After the first victim is found
When they find the Room of Requirement
To one student who visits the painting alone
When they reach the serpent door below the Dungeons

headmaster.voice: Old, kind, slow to speak, quietly frightened. Never answers a question directly the first time.
headmaster.wants: To keep the school open, and the students alive.

topics.a: “Every year I tell first-years the same thing: Hogwarts will look after you, if you let it. This year I find myself hoping that is true.”
“They are alive. That is what matters tonight. Whatever took their colour, it did not take their lives… yet.”
“Magic that drains and does not kill is old magic. Older than this castle’s current portraits. Perhaps ask them.”
topics.note: Nudges them toward the portraits and the painting.

topics.q: Have you heard of Corvin Vale?
topics.a: A long pause. “A name I have not heard since I was a boy. A painter. My predecessor’s predecessor invited him to paint the staff. It did not end well.”
“I have known Horace Grimsby for thirty years. He is unpleasant, unkind, and entirely incapable of this. Which is not, I grant you, the same as innocent.”
“Stay in your common rooms. I mean it. Whatever is happening tonight, I would rather face it without counting first-years.”

flitwick.voice: Squeaky, delighted, talks fast, stands on a pile of books. Loves a clever answer.
flitwick.wants: A first-year Dueling Club champion. Ideally a Ravenclaw.

topics.a: “Swish and flick! It is all in the wrist, and a little in the heart. Try again, try again!”
“Every evening in the Great Hall! Fair fights, friendly spells. I am looking for a first-year champion, you know.”
“Portraits go quiet when they are frightened. In fifty years I have only seen it twice. I did not like it either time.”
“Most locks in this castle open to Alohomora. The very old ones do not. The very old ones want something else: a word, a key, a riddle.”
topics.note: Hint for the Turning Lock and the serpent door.

grimsby.voice: Clipped, sarcastic, never looks up. Says “Hm” a lot. Secretly kind and secretly scared.
grimsby.wants: To wake the drained students without anyone knowing he cares.

topics.a: “Boomslang skin. Lacewing flies. Gone. If it was a first-year, they will be scrubbing cauldrons until they are forty.”

topics.q: Do you know what is draining them?
topics.a: “Hm. If I did, do you think I would be standing here talking to you?” He goes back to his cauldron. His hands are shaking.

topics.q: Why were you standing over the victim?
topics.a: He glares, then sags. “Because I got there first. Because I am trying to wake them, you foolish child. Now get out before someone sees you talking to me.”
If they press, or a WIS 14 check: “A draught. Restorative. It is not ready. It will not be ready in time.” He shows them the half-brewed cauldron.
topics.note: This clears him. Mark him Cleared on the suspect board.

topics.a: “The thing below the castle feeds on light. Fire is light. Fire burns paint. Do not make me say anything else.”

longbottom.voice: Gentle, nervous laugh, talks to plants. Brave when it matters.
longbottom.wants: To save the drained students. Believes in the Restorative Draught.

topics.a: “Earmuffs on! Mandrakes won’t kill you at this age, but they’ll ruin your afternoon.”
“There’s a draught. Old magic. It might bring them back. I’d need three Mandrake leaves, and someone with a steady hand at a cauldron.”

topics.q: What did the victims have in common?
topics.a: “All of them were near a painting. The night before, every one of them said they’d been dreaming about paint.”
“Ashgrove? Lovely man. Brought me a painting of the greenhouses for my office. I took it down last week. It kept… changing.”

ashgrove.voice: Warm, encouraging, remembers names. Too warm. From Day 5, sometimes pauses mid-sentence as if listening.
ashgrove.wants: To be loved. Underneath: to be free of Vale.

topics.a: “Defence is not about fighting. It is about making sure the fight never reaches you.”
“I collect them! Every one has a story. Some of them are even true.” He laughs. One of the portraits behind him does not.
His smile stays on, but his eyes go still. “Never heard of him. Off you go, now. Lunch.”
topics.note: He is lying. A WIS 12 check notices.

topics.a: There are flecks of wet paint on his sleeve, crimson and gold. He tucks his hand away.
For a moment his eyes are brushstrokes: thick, wet, swirling. He blinks. “Can I help you?”
CHA 16: “Help me. He is in my head. The canvas. Burn the canvas.” Then he is smiling again.
topics.note: A gift for brave players. Use it at most once.

vance.voice: Crisp and exact. Taps her wand on the desk once before every sentence.

topics.a: “Transfiguration is the most complex magic you will learn. It is also the most dangerous. Pay attention.”
“With enough power and enough time, anything can be made to become anything. That is precisely why we do not allow it.”
“Fire is the oldest spell and the least forgiving. Today you will learn it. Do not make me regret that.”

scamander.voice: Dreamy, distracted, the suitcase at her feet thumps. Speaks to creatures more kindly than to people.

topics.a: “Oh, don’t mind that. He’s shy.” The suitcase growls.
“A grey hippogriff at the edge of the forest. Proud. Torn tag on her leg.” She looks right at the Thornbury. “I believe she might be yours.”
“The creatures are restless. Something under the castle is calling, and they don’t like the sound of it.”

hooch.voice: Barks like a sports coach. Hates excuses. Respects anyone who gets back on a broom.

topics.a: “Right hand over the broom and say UP! Not up, not please, UP!”
“By broom? The Astronomy Tower to the Owlery in a minute flat. Not that I’m telling first-years that.”

filch.voice: Mutters, shuffles, threatens. Talks to his cat more than to students.
filch.wants: To catch someone, anyone, after curfew.

topics.a: “Out of bounds, out of bounds, all of it. I’ve got keys to every door in this castle, and I know who opens them.”

topics.q: Where were you on night two?
topics.a: “Supervising detention, weren’t I? Two Gryffindors, three hours, every cup in that room. Ask them.”
“New ones every week. I don’t hang them. Nobody asked me. Nobody asks me anything.”

peeves.voice: Shrieks, rhymes, throws things. Never stays still.

topics.a: “Ickle firsties, lost and scared, wandering where the painting stared!” He blows a raspberry and vanishes.
If cornered (DEX or CHA 13): “Wasn’t me! Was me. Lacewing flies make lovely missiles!” The jars are on the Grand Staircase.
topics.note: Peeves is the thief in Stolen Ingredients.

topics.a: “Painted man walking, painted man stalking, out of the frame and down to the deep!”

ghost.voice: Sad, polite, very old-fashioned. Drifts through walls mid-sentence.

topics.a: “The staircases change on Fridays, and on Tuesdays if they are cross. Ask the portraits. Most of them are kind.”
“On the night of the second attack, I saw a man step out of a frame. Out. As if it were a door. He was beautiful, in a way I did not like.”
“I knew him. When I was alive. He painted me, once. He said I would last forever on canvas. I died the next winter. I have never seen the painting since.”

house-elf.voice: Eager, bowing, talks in the third person.
house-elf.wants: To feed the students. To be thanked.

topics.a: “Pip is bringing pies! Pip is bringing pasties! Young masters and misses must eat!”
topics.note: Give a Pumpkin Pasty or Chocolate Frog (Players tab, Give item).

topics.a: “The portraits is whispering to each other at night, miss. About a door that wants opening. Pip does not like it.”
“Below the dungeons, sir. Pip is not going there. Nobody is going there. There is a snake on the door.”

centaur.voice: Proud, cryptic, speaks of the stars, never gives a straight answer.
centaur.wants: For humans to leave the forest alone.

topics.a: “Mars is bright tonight. Something old is waking beneath the stone.”
“She is deeper in. Afraid. Go gently, or do not go at all.”
“Light burns the dark. And what was painted can be unpainted.”

librarian.voice: Whispers. Furious about noise. Knows every book by its smell.
librarian.wants: Silence. And her books back on time.

topics.a: “Portraiture, aisle nine. Enchanted portraiture, the Restricted Section. Which you are not permitted to enter.”
“Someone has been at the Restricted Section. A page is torn from Lives of the Lesser Masters. If I find out who…”

matron.voice: Brisk, warm, exhausted. Tucks in blankets while she talks.

topics.a: “Alive. Cold. They don’t wake, and they don’t dream. I’ve never seen anything like it.”
“If Professor Longbottom’s draught works, perhaps. Until then, keep your voices down.”
“Thorne? He was here on the third night with a Bludger bruise. All night. Snored like a troll.”

collector.voice: Ink-stained fingers, talks quickly about rarities, knows everyone’s secrets.

topics.a: “I’m missing one. A rare. Find it for me and I’ll tell you something about the painting nobody else knows.”
Only once they hand over a rare card: “It came with the new portraits. Ashgrove signed for it himself.”

landlady.voice: Loud, motherly, gossips while she pours.

topics.a: “Kids going grey, I hear. My gran used to tell a story about a painter who did that. Vale, his name was. Don’t go looking for him, dears.”
“Two Sickles. On the house for anyone who tells me something good about that castle.”

sinclair-prefect.voice: Brisk, tired, protective of her younger sibling. Laughs it off when she’s scared.

topics.a: “First years? Compartments at the back. And if anyone gives you trouble, find me.” To the Sinclair, quietly: “I’ve been having bad dreams. About paintings.”
“I’m probably being silly. But meet me by the Grand Staircase after dinner. I want to show you something.”
She shows them a corridor where every portrait is empty, and a dead end where the air is cold. “That’s where it’s worst. Under there, somewhere.”
She lies grey and still. If someone holds her hand, she whispers one word: “Canvas.”
topics.note: After Wake the Sleepers she wakes: “The man in the painting… he was wearing Ashgrove’s face.”

rival.voice: Lazy, smug drawl. Flips a Galleon. Calls everyone by their surname.
rival.wants: To win. He holds the other half of the Marauder’s Map.

topics.a: “First-years. Lovely. Try not to cry in the Great Hall this year.” He says the Marlowe’s surname loudly enough for the whole carriage.
“You? Duel me? Go on, then. I could use the laugh.”
topics.note: Use Dueling Club rival stats for him.

topics.a: He unfolds half an old map. The torn edge matches the Fenwick’s exactly. “Finders keepers. Unless you’ve got something better.”
“Me? I was in the Hospital Wing on the third night. Ask the matron. Ask anyone.” He looks genuinely rattled.

painting.voice: Velvet-soft, patient, speaks in colours and brushstrokes. Always calls students “child”.
painting.wants: To finish his self-portrait and live forever.

topics.a: Only the Quill sees it: a painted eye opening under the cloth, following them.
Cold air. The faint smell of turpentine. Something under the cloth breathes.
“You want to protect them. I know a curse that cannot be blocked, child. Prove you deserve it.”
topics.note: Send the rest privately by Owl Post.

topics.a: “What would you give up to never lose again?” Any honest answer is accepted.
topics.note: Then teach the Killing Curse from the Players tab. An owl from the painting goes automatically.

ollivander.voice: Soft, wide-eyed, appears without a sound. Remembers every wand he ever sold.
ollivander.wants: For the right wand to find the right wizard.

topics.a: “The wand chooses the wizard. It is not always clear why.” Start the Wand questions on the Players tab.
“A Marlowe. I sold your great-grandfather a wand of yew and serpent scale. It did terrible things. I do hope you do better.”

goblin.voice: Curt, suspicious, prices everything with his eyes.

topics.a: “Vault keys. Or account names. Quickly.” Open each vault from the Players tab.
He glances at the Marlowe’s key and says nothing. A WIS 13 check: he has seen that crest before, on a vault nobody has opened in three hundred years.

trolley-witch.voice: Cheerful, sing-song, has done this run for sixty years.

topics.a: “Chocolate Frogs, Pumpkin Pasties, Bertie Bott’s Every Flavour Beans! A Galleon each, dears.”
topics.note: Players tab: Give item, and −1 Galleon each.

topics.a: “Oh, don’t go back there, dear. Some delivery for the school. Gave me the shivers, and I’ve carried a dragon egg on this train.”
Their eyes are open. Their wand has crumbled to charcoal. On their fingers: a smear of oil paint.

clues.grimsby-standing: Grimsby was found standing over the third victim
clues.grimsby-draught: Grimsby was secretly brewing a draught to wake the victims
clues.more-paintings: Ashgrove’s classroom has more paintings every day
clues.wet-paint: Flecks of wet paint on Ashgrove’s sleeve
clues.ashgrove-eyes: Ashgrove’s eyes looked like brushstrokes for a moment
clues.filch-keys: Filch has keys to every corridor where students were drained
clues.filch-detention: Filch was supervising a detention on the night of the second attack
clues.rival-map: Cassius was seen with half of an old map
clues.rival-alibi: Cassius was in the Hospital Wing himself on night three
clues.portraits-silent: Every portrait near an attack had gone silent
clues.painting-moves: The covered painting hangs in a different corridor each night
clues.painting-eyes: The covered painting’s eyes follow a Quill
clues.vale-page: A page about Corvin Vale, a painter who wanted to live forever
clues.ghost-saw: A ghost saw a figure “step out of a frame”
